title: astra.registry.cutover/1
description:
log/cutover.json — the marker that says cutover has happened, added by the cutover commit and by nothing else (contract ROLL-33; B.4). From that commit the plugins service is the only publication channel.

THE FILE IS THE FACT. MIG-1, ID-25 and registry plan BOT-72 all key on "`log/cutover.json` is on `main`", so a reader outside this repository can settle the question with one path and no API: the marker's PRESENCE is what those rules test. `cutover_at` is the moment, for the arithmetic MIG-1 needs — `grandfathered` until the LATER of the deadline and cutover — and it is the cutover commit's own time (registry plan M-T6.2).

EXACTLY TWO MEMBERS, and `$comment` is NOT among them, for the reason schema/deadline-v1.json gives at length: B.4 fixes the member set, the service parses this record, and a member one party admits and another refuses is a two-way-test failure (§0.8) discovered in production.

WHOLE SECONDS, AND `Z` (§0.7). A pattern cannot tell a real date from `2026-02-31T00:00:00Z`; tools/validate.mjs round-trips the value through Date, which is the other half of the check.

WHAT NOTHING HERE CAN CHECK. That `cutover_at` is in fact the commit's time is not a property of the file, and neither is ROLL-33's "only the cutover commit adds it" — both are statements about git. The second is B-T3.6's and BOT-54's to enforce on the pull-request door; the first would need a reader that knows which commit added the path (bot/detectors.mjs's `addedBy` is the shape of it) and today nobody does. Recorded as a gap rather than implied by this file's existence.

cutover_at.$comment: The cutover commit's time. MIG-1 grandfathers a listing until the later of this and the deadline, so a marker committed before the deadline changes no listing's state on its own — it is the deadline that then decides.
